usage.dataset: Isopedia human long-read isoform atlas (table_wide2 build, 869 PacBio/ONT samples); per-transcript usage = that transcript's read-weighted share of its gene, aggregated over all samples in which the gene was detected
usage.cv: GroupKFold(5) grouped by gene; alphas chosen per fold by RidgeCV [10.0, 3162.2776601683795]
usage.target: transcript usage fraction (raw, not logit) so that ridge, the mechanistic model and the baselines are all on one scale

app12.note: the app's mechanistic co-transcriptional splicing model can only be evaluated on the 12 genes for which data/splice_data.json carries a hand-built gene structure, so this block is restricted to them; MaxEntScan donor/acceptor scores here are the ones already in data/splice_data.json (maxentpy, Yeo & Burge 2004); the measured target there is every GENCODE v49 transcript of the 12 genes from the genome-wide Isopedia query table, and `ridge_compact` is the genome-wide ridge refit on only the features derivable from data/splice_data.json, with these 12 genes' loci removed from its training set

methods.text: Measured isoform usage from the Isopedia human long-read isoform atlas (/data/mdl_data/hyu/projects/public_isoform/isopedia, table_wide2 build - the same build pipeline/isopedia/ uses: an 18,839-gene panel, 105,837 catalogue isoforms, 869 public PacBio/ONT samples, 32.7M (isoform, sample) rows in table_wide2/context_table.parquet). Each row's usage is that splice-pattern isoform's share of its gene's reads in that sample; transcripts sharing an intron chain are collapsed and whatever is left over sits in an other:<gene> row. Per transcript we sum usage over all samples and divide by the gene total INCLUDING that other row, so a gene's modelled fractions sum to 1 minus the unmodelled remainder rather than being inflated to 1. Loci are kept only if seen in >=20 samples and if >=2 of their transcripts survive the filters.

Per-transcript, all interpretable. Exon/intron counts and lengths, alternative-event flags (cassette skip / alt 5'ss / alt 3'ss / alt first exon, each relative to the gene's longest transcript as a structural reference chosen without looking at usage) and the distance from the gene's dominant annotated TSS are computed here from table_wide2/isoforms.parquet exon coordinates. GC, 5' UTR and ORF length, uAUG count, NMD/PTC flag, intron retention, TSS CpG/TATA and polyA-signal flags come from table_wide2/catalog_features.parquet.

MaxEntScan is recomputed genome-wide here with the same scorer pipeline/splice/build_splice.py uses - maxentpy (X. Dong), which ships the original Yeo & Burge (2004) matrices: score5 on the 9-mer -3..+6 around the donor, score3 on the 23-mer -20..+3 around the acceptor. Both documented reference examples are re-validated at the start of every run and the run aborts if they do not reproduce. The windows are read by random access out of a faidx-indexed GRCh38 FASTA rather than from the Ensembl REST API, which does not scale to 730k introns; the exon-coordinate convention is chosen empirically as the offset that yields canonical GT..AG, and the chosen offset and its GT..AG rate are recorded in pipeline/splice_ridge/work/maxent_meta.json. Pangolin splice-site probabilities from table_wide2/splice (meta.json model=pangolin) are kept alongside as separate features, never merged with the MaxEntScan ones.

RidgeCV over 40 alphas in 1e-3..1e4 on z-scored features; target is the raw usage fraction (not its logit) so that ridge, the mechanistic model and every baseline live on one scale. Cross-validation is GroupKFold(5) grouped by gene, so no gene appears in both train and test. Coefficient CIs are 2.5/97.5 percentiles of 200 bootstraps that resample whole genes.

expected(gene, values()) from app/src/splice/model_exact.js after calibrate(data), at the app's default parameters, run under node (pipeline/splice_ridge/mech_eval.mjs). Nothing in it is fitted to the Isopedia usage.

Every pair of transcripts inside a gene whose measured usage differs by more than 1e-6; a method scores 1 if it orders the pair correctly, 0.5 if it ties them. 0.5 is therefore the no-information baseline.

caveats: Splice-site strength enters twice and the two are not interchangeable: MaxEntScan scores the 9-mer/23-mer windows alone, while Pangolin already encodes much of the wider sequence context.
The genome-wide fit is restricted to transcripts with a Pangolin score, i.e. the Isopedia catalogue's spliced multi-exon isoforms; single-isoform loci carry no usage information and are dropped.

Usage is pooled over a heterogeneous panel of public long-read samples (many tissues, two platforms). It is a panel-average usage, not a usage in any one tissue, and long-read 5'/3' completeness differs between platforms.
The mechanistic-model comparison is on 12 genes only, which is far too few to separate the methods; treat its numbers as a sanity check, not a benchmark.

'Read support' (number of samples in which a transcript is detected) is NOT an independent confound: it is computed from the same per-sample usage values as the target, so a transcript seen in more samples necessarily has a larger usage sum. It is reported to show how much of the within-gene signal is simply abundance, and must not be read as a model that beats the others. The non-circular confounds are transcript length and exon count.
CAGE promoter weights (data/tss_weights.json, FANTOM5) exist only for the app's genes, so the genome-wide promoter baseline is the annotation-derived dominant-TSS share instead.
